summary: Improve frontline journeys, complaint handling, and customer effort measures. Explore the practical five-day service experience management course.
lede: Service experience management designs and oversees customer-facing interactions across channels to identify friction and improve handoffs. For customer service managers, service quality analysts and channel leaders, the course develops skills in journey mapping, service blueprinting and complaint handling. Participants also practice classifying customer feedback, measuring customer effort and assigning follow-up actions, with introductory coverage of AI-assisted sentiment analysis.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who oversee or improve customer-facing service journeys, complaint resolution, and service quality across physical, digital, and contact-centre channels. This course is designed for: Customer Service Managers overseeing frontline service standards and complaint resolution. Service Quality Analysts reviewing customer feedback and recurring service failures. Branch Managers improving in-person journeys, queue handling, and service handoffs. Contact-Centre Leaders monitoring resolution quality and repeat-contact patterns. Customer Experience Analysts mapping journeys and tracking customer effort measures. Complaint Resolution Specialists investigating cases and coordinating customer responses. Digital Service Managers improving online journeys and channel handoffs. Public-Facing Supervisors coaching teams on consistent service recovery. Voice-of-Customer Leads assigning feedback themes to operational owners. Service Operations Managers prioritising cross-channel improvements and reporting progress.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with customer-facing service operations, service quality, or complaint handling is recommended. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with Excel access for the spreadsheet-based exercises; AI and automated analytics topics are introduced conceptually rather than implemented.
